dict.string: OpenDisk measures how much disk space each folder on your Mac uses. Access to your music library lets OpenDisk include it in your storage breakdown - for example, showing that your Music library takes up 15 GB so you can decide what to clean up. OpenDisk only reads file names and sizes; it never plays, uploads, or modifies your music.

OpenDisk measures how much disk space each folder on your Mac uses. Access to your Desktop folder lets OpenDisk include it in your storage breakdown - for example, showing that your Desktop takes up 3 GB so you can decide what to clean up. OpenDisk only reads file names and sizes; it never uploads or modifies your files.

OpenDisk measures how much disk space each folder on your Mac uses. Access to your Documents folder lets OpenDisk include it in your storage breakdown - for example, showing that your Documents folder takes up 10 GB so you can decide what to clean up. OpenDisk only reads file names and sizes; it never uploads or modifies your files.

OpenDisk measures how much disk space each folder on your Mac uses. Access to your Downloads folder lets OpenDisk include it in your storage breakdown - for example, showing that your Downloads folder takes up 8 GB so you can decide what to clean up. OpenDisk only reads file names and sizes; it never uploads or modifies your files.

OpenDisk measures how much disk space each folder uses. Access to network volumes lets OpenDisk scan drives you connect over the network - for example, showing that a NAS share holds 500 GB of backups. OpenDisk only reads file names and sizes; it never uploads or modifies your files.

OpenDisk measures how much disk space each folder on your Mac uses. Access to your photo library lets OpenDisk include it in your storage breakdown - for example, showing that your Photos library takes up 20 GB so you can decide what to clean up. OpenDisk only reads file names and sizes; it never views, uploads, or modifies your photos.

OpenDisk measures how much disk space each folder uses. Access to removable volumes lets OpenDisk scan external drives and USB disks you plug in - for example, showing that an external drive holds 200 GB of old projects. OpenDisk only reads file names and sizes; it never uploads or modifies your files.
